correctness.rationale: Full block multiplication proves commutation iff AE=DB and center A=B=0. For b=1 rank-one outer product equality yields precisely three types of clique components and AC property. For b>=2 the common-u / square-zero rank-one middle operator T=u phi constructs a noncentral commuting path of length at most three with no field-size exception; a=1 or c=1 provides a common noncentral commuter; the injective/surjective witness proves diameter at least three when a,c>=b. The proof verifies all quantifiers for q any prime power; direct 13-case independently constructed finite graphs corroborate, but do not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: The result gives a structural dichotomy for all positive triple block sizes over all finite fields, a complete decomposition into explicitly sized components at the disconnected boundary, and a uniform sharp three-step routing argument with infinite exact diameter-two and diameter-three regimes. These graph properties are natural for algebraic groups and not determined by the previously known maximum Lie breadth or character degrees; the unclassified intermediate exact-diameter region is disclosed.
